question: Which of the following classical dance form is associated with Kerala?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Mohiniyattam**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mohiniyattam** is a classical dance form from Kerala, India.
 
• It is known for its graceful and feminine movements, often performed as a solo recital by women.
 
• The dance form is deeply rooted in the **Lasya** style, which represents the feminine and tender aspects of dance.
 
• Mohiniyattam combines elements of **Bharatanatyam** and **Kathakali**, two other major classical dance forms from Southern India.
 
• The word "Mohiniyattam" comes from "Mohini," a female avatar of the Hindu god Vishnu, and "attam," meaning dance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kerala** is also home to other classical dance forms like **Kathakali** and **Theyyam**.
 
• Mohiniyattam costumes are traditionally white or off-white with gold borders, known as **Kasavu** sarees.
 
• The dance form has a rich repertoire of **stories from Hindu mythology**, often focusing on the themes of love and devotion.
 
• Mohiniyattam was revived in the 20th century by the efforts of artists and scholars who aimed to preserve this cultural heritage.
 
• It is recognized as one of the eight classical dance forms of India by the Sangeet Natak Akademi.
